title: Honor Father and Mother
kjv_text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.
summary: Positive duty of honor toward both parents, with a stated reward: long tenure in the land. The only commandment with an attached promise.
original_audience: Primarily adult Israelites responsible for aging parents' maintenance, not small children being told to obey.
immediate_context: Fifth commandment, opening the second tablet's social duties; enforced elsewhere by capital statutes against striking or cursing parents (Ex 21:15,17).
historical_context: In a society without pensions, 'honor' meant material support of the old. Wisdom literature and ANE instruction texts (e.g., Egyptian Instruction of Any) carry the same duty. Jesus attacks the corban loophole by which dedicated funds escaped the obligation (Mark 7:9-13).
penalty: None here (reward stated instead); striking or cursing a parent is death (Ex 21:15,17); the incorrigible son is stoned (Deut 21:18-21).
exceptions: Jesus repeatedly relativizes family duty toward himself (Matt 10:35-37, Luke 14:26).
nt_passages: Ephesians 6:1-3 — Paul quotes it as 'the first commandment with promise'
Mark 7:9-13 — Jesus condemns the corban loophole
Matthew 10:35-37 — 'he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me'
Luke 14:26 — 'if any man... hate not his father, and mother... he cannot be my disciple'

internal_contradictions.issue: How should parents be treated? Honor them (here) vs. Jesus requiring disciples to 'hate' father and mother.
Is it OK to call your father 'father'? Matthew 23:9 says call no man father — awkward for the commandment's wording.

usofc_implementation: The Filial Piety Act: adult children file annual Parental Maintenance Statements; support is payroll-deducted like a second social security aimed backward. Public dishonor of a parent (defined by regulation, 40 pages) is a civil infraction ladder that tops out, theoretically, at the Incorrigibility Statute — never yet invoked, always available.
constitutional_analogue: Filial responsibility laws exist in ~30 US states, rarely enforced; the USofC enforces them universally and criminally.
scene_ideas: An estranged daughter's maintenance garnishment funding the abusive father she fled.
A DFO mediator processing a corban-style trust — funds 'dedicated to the Church' to starve out a parent — with Mark 7 read aloud by opposing counsel.
The first prosecutor to actually file under the Incorrigibility Statute becoming a national crisis.
satirical_uses: The promise clause is administered literally: verified honorers receive an actuarial bonus called Longevity Credit, paid, with no irony, from the estates of the dishonoring.
bureaucratic_uses: Dishonor infraction schedule with point system
